title: Recording: Who Can See It by George Harrison | 1972
content:
Apple Studios, London
Producer: George Harrison
Engineer: Phil McDonald

George Harrison recorded ‘Who Can See It’, for his fourth solo album Living In The Material World, on 13 October 1972.

‘Who Can See It’ was listed as ‘My Life Belongs To Me’ on the tape box.

The basic track had Klaus Voormann’s bass guitar on track one, and Jim Keltner’s drums on two and three. Harrison’s electric guitar, fed through a revolving Leslie speaker, was on tracks five and six, and his vocals on 10. Nicky Hopkins’ piano was on tracks seven and eight, and Gary Wright’s organ and harmonium were on 11 and 12.

Ninety-four takes of ‘Who Can See It’ were recorded, although many were incomplete. The arrangement took shape throughout the session, and was mostly in place by take 71. Take 94 was marked best and became the album master.

During the session the musicians also jammed versions of ‘At The Hop’ by Danny And The Juniors and ‘When I Paint My Masterpiece’ by Bob Dylan.

This was the final recording session for Living In The Material World to feature the full band. Subsequent sessions were for overdubs only.
